precepts.text: Into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people; even the priests sinned.
precepts.point: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God. Christ took away the first covenant to establish the second, and we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. Men had been sacrificing since the days of Adam; when Christ came, one sacrifice ended it, because that lamb had no blemish. The law of sacrifice was always temporary, a shadow of good things to come, and the good thing that came was Christ.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
Even the priest that is anointed committed sin, according to the sin of the people, and had to bring a young bullock without blemish unto the Lord for a sin offering. Hebrews shows the order of the service: “the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people”.

Not without blood, offered for himself and for the errors of the people: the high priest had sins of his own to atone for before the people’s. The sin offering of Leviticus 4 covered the anointed priest as well as the soul that sinned through ignorance.

precepts.text: Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; he taketh away the first covenant to establish the second, and this man offered one sacrifice for sins for ever and sat down.
precepts.point: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God. Christ took away the first covenant to establish the second, and we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. Men had been sacrificing since the days of Adam; when Christ came, one sacrifice ended it, because that lamb had no blemish. The law of sacrifice was always temporary, a shadow of good things to come, and the good thing that came was Christ.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
The people got redundant with it: “every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins”. They kept sinning and kept bringing sacrifices instead of repenting, thinking it was okay to sin as long as the offerings kept coming. It is the same spirit today, wicked all weekend and a hundred dollars in the plate on Sunday; the Most High does not want your money, He wants you to repent. Only you can put away your sins, when you repent and stop sinning.

“Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law; Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” Christ took away the first covenant to establish the second, “By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

“But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God”. Men had been sacrificing since the days of Adam; when Christ came, one sacrifice ended it, because that lamb had no blemish. The law of sacrifice in Leviticus 4 was always temporary, a shadow of good things to come, and the good thing that came was Christ.

precepts.text: If thou sayest, behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? The excuse of ignorance does not stand before him.
precepts.point: Saying we knew it not does not stand before the Most High. Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it, and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? A lot of people say they never heard this truth when they heard it and did not want to apply it. The Most High knows the things that come into your mind, every one of them; he created us and knows us better than we know ourselves, and he knows whether you sinned through ignorance or willfully.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
Saying we knew it not does not stand before the Most High. “If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?”

A lot of people say they never heard this truth when they heard it and did not want to apply it. Some of what is called ignorance is not ignorance; it is complacency, a lack of faith, a mind not in the spirit. He that pondereth the heart knows whether the ruler sinned through ignorance or willfully, and renders to every man according to his works.

precepts.why:
“Thus have ye said, O house of Israel: for I know the things that come into your mind, every one of them.”

The Most High knows the things that come into your mind, every one of them. He created us and knows us better than we know ourselves, and He knows the spirit behind the sin: whether you sinned through ignorance, as the ruler in Leviticus 4, or willfully.

precepts.text: Sin committed by ignorance was atoned and forgiven, one law for him that is born among Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them.
precepts.point: Presumptuously means impulsive and willful: no boundaries, doing things without seeking counsel, led by your own mind, your own opinion, your own emotions instead of leaning on the leadership the Most High set in place. Peter marks that spirit: they walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, despise government, presumptuous are they, selfwilled, not afraid to speak evil of dignities. Despising government, gossiping and murmuring against leadership, and refusing to gather with the body is that same dangerous spirit; the Lord said gather yourselves together, O nation not desired, and he works through spiritual men as he did through Moses and Aaron.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
Numbers 15 lays the two ways side by side, and this is the first, sin by ignorance: “if ought be committed by ignorance without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall offer one young bullock for a burnt offering, for a sweet savour unto the Lord, with his meat offering, and his drink offering, according to the manner, and one kid of the goats for a sin offering. And the priest shall make an atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and it shall be forgiven them; for it is ignorance”.

The same for one soul: “if any soul sin through ignorance, then he shall bring a she goat of the first year for a sin offering. And the priest shall make an atonement for the soul that sinneth ignorantly, when he sinneth by ignorance before the Lord, to make an atonement for him; and it shall be forgiven him.” That is the ruler’s kid of the goats in Leviticus 4: atonement made, reconciliation with the Lord, and forgiveness of sins.

“Ye shall have one law for him that sinneth through ignorance, both for him that is born among the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them.” One law for the born Israelite and the stranger alike.

precepts.text: The soul that doeth ought presumptuously reproacheth the Lord and shall be cut off; he hath despised the word of the Lord.
precepts.point: Presumptuously means impulsive and willful: no boundaries, doing things without seeking counsel, led by your own mind, your own opinion, your own emotions instead of leaning on the leadership the Most High set in place. Peter marks that spirit: they walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, despise government, presumptuous are they, selfwilled, not afraid to speak evil of dignities. note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
This is the other way, set right against the sin of ignorance: “the soul that doeth ought presumptuously, whether he be born in the land, or a stranger, the same reproacheth the Lord; and that soul shall be cut off from among his people. Because he hath despised the word of the Lord, and hath broken his commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off; his iniquity shall be upon him.”

There is no kid of the goats for this one. Presumptuously means impulsive and willful: no boundaries, doing things without seeking counsel, led by your own mind, your own opinion, your own emotions instead of leaning on the leadership the Most High set in place. He hath despised the word of the Lord, and his iniquity shall be upon him.

precepts.why:
Peter marks the presumptuous spirit: “them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.”

Despising government, gossiping and murmuring against leadership, and refusing to gather with the body is that same dangerous spirit Numbers 15 says shall be cut off. The Lord said gather yourselves together, O nation not desired, and He works through spiritual men as He did through Moses and Aaron. The selfwilled man, led by his own mind and not afraid to speak evil of dignities, is not sinning through ignorance.

precepts.text: The man gathering sticks on the Sabbath was kept in ward until the mind of the Lord was declared, and the Lord said he shall surely be put to death.
precepts.point: That is the judgment on the willful: if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins. That man knew the law; it was not ignorance, it was blatant. The Lord knoweth all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts; he knoweth your inventions and what ye think in your heart, even them that sin and would hide their sin. Sin willfully and your grace period is up.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
The man found gathering sticks upon the Sabbath day shows the presumptuous side, immediately after that law was spoken. When they found him, “they that found him gathering sticks brought him unto Moses and Aaron, and unto all the congregation. And they put him in ward, because it was not declared what should be done to him.”

They did not kill him right away; they put him in ward, and Moses got direction from the Lord. “And the Lord said unto Moses, The man shall be surely put to death: all the congregation shall stone him with stones without the camp.” And all the congregation brought him without the camp and stoned him, as the Lord commanded Moses.

That man knew the law; it was not ignorance, it was blatant. There was no offering for him, the way there was a kid of the goats for the ruler who sinned through ignorance.

The same Lord that made heaven and earth by the word knows all the works of men, their imaginations, their thoughts, and their hearts. So He knows whether a ruler did somewhat through ignorance or willfully; nothing about the sin is hid from Him.

“Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.”

Nothing willful is hid from Him. The one who sins and then says he knew it not, hiding his sin under ignorance, is known for what he is. He that pondereth the heart considers it, and that is why the law separates the sin of ignorance, which has its atonement, from the presumptuous sin, which is cut off.

points: The sin offering is for a soul that sins through ignorance against any of the commandments. You sin through ignorance when you get complacent: it was a double Sabbath and you forgot, and you bought or sold something you were not supposed to; an honest mistake. Even then it was not a verbal sorry; you literally brought an offering for your mistake.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

points: If the whole congregation sin through ignorance and the thing be hid from the eyes of the assembly, pay attention to the key word: they have done somewhat against the commandments. It says somewhat because the Lord knows your heart, and the heart is deceitful and wicked above all things; you say you sinned through ignorance, and the Lord knows whether that is so.

points: When the sin is known, the congregation offers a young bullock; the elders lay their hands upon its head before the Lord, the blood is sprinkled seven times before the vail and put on the horns of the altar, all the fat is burned, and the bullock is burned without the camp as the first: and the priest shall make an atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them.

points: Even the priests and the rulers had to offer for their own sins. That is the reason the law of sacrifice had to be done away with: the high priest, Christ, came and gave one offering, as Hebrews lays out, and he was done; he did not do it for millenniums, he came one time.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

points: If any one of the common people sin through ignorance, his offering was a kid of the goats or a lamb, a female without blemish; he laid his hand upon the head of the sin offering, the blood went on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, the fat was burned for a sweet savour, and the priest made an atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.
